classification.difficultyReason: Student must read k from the labelled point on the graph, then reframe k as the prism's base area and apply a rectangle area formula (part a) and a triangle area formula (part b) to find the missing dimension. This is a linked procedure with one reinterpretation step, like the 'gradient as cross-sectional area' idea in p12-q10 but with the connection less signposted and no hint.

content.prompt: The graphs show how the volume $V$ m³ of a prism is related to its height $h$ m by $V=kh$, where $k$ is a constant.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The prism has a rectangular base that is 1.5 m wide. Find the length of the base.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}k&=\frac{27}{6}\\k&=4.5\end{align*}$$
The gradient $k$ is the cross-sectional area, so the base area is $4.5\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{length}\times1.5&=4.5\\\text{length}&=\frac{4.5}{1.5}\\&=3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The prism has a triangular base with a base length of 5 m. Find the perpendicular height of the triangle.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}k&=\frac{30}{4}\\k&=7.5\end{align*}$$
The gradient $k$ is the cross-sectional area, so the triangle's area is $7.5\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac12\times5\times\text{height}&=7.5\\2.5\times\text{height}&=7.5\\\text{height}&=3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
